For a smooth quasi-projective surface $V$ with $\overline\kappa(V)\ge 0$ and non-maximal logarithmic Albanese dimension, the logarithmic Albanese map has image of dimension $\le 1$. By the logarithmic generic vanishing theorem and the structure of such fibrations (Chen), one obtains the optimal linear bound $\overline P_1(V)\ge \overline q(V)-1$. Sharpness is exhibited by suitable $\mathbb{C}^*$-bundles or logarithmic fibrations over curves where $h^0(X,K_X+D)=h^0(X,\Omega^1_X(\log D))-1$. Thus $f(q)=q-1$.

we have $h^0(\Omega^1_X(\log D)) = h^0(\Omega^1_B) = g(B)$ (if the ruled surface is "sufficiently twisted"). Let me verify: for $X = \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E})$, $D$ a section, $\Omega^1_X(\log D)$ fits in
$0 \to p^*\Omega^1_B \to \Omega^1_X(\log D) \to \Omega^1_{X/C}(\log D) \to 0$.
The relative part $\Omega^1_{X/C}(\log D)$ restricted to a fiber is $\Omega^1_{\mathbb{P}^1}(\log\{\infty\}) = \mathcal{O}(-1)$, which has no sections. So if the ruled surface is chosen so that $p_*\Omega^1_{X/C}(\log D) = 0$ and $R^1p_*$ doesn't contribute to $h^0$, then $h^0(\Omega^1_X(\log D)) = h^0(\Omega^1_B) = g(B)$.

For example, take $X = \mathbb{P}(L \oplus \mathcal{O})$ with $\deg L > 0$, and $D = D_\infty$ (the section corresponding to $L \oplus \mathcal{O} \to L$). Then $\Omega^1_{X/B}(\log D) = \mathcal{O}_X(-D) \otimes ...$ Actually, the normal bundle of $D$ is $L$, so the relative log differentials might be $\mathcal{O}(-D) \otimes p^*L$ or similar. In any case, if $L$ is sufficiently positive, there are no global relative log 1-forms.

So $\overline{q}(V) = g(B) =: q$. Now what is $\overline{P}_1(V) = h^0(K_X + D)$? For $X = \mathbb{P}(L \oplus \mathcal{O})$, $K_X = \mathcal{O}(-2) \otimes p^*(L \otimes K_B)$, and $D = D_\infty \sim \mathcal{O}(1) \otimes p^*L^{-1}$. So $K_X + D = \mathcal{O}(-1) \otimes p^*K_B$. Then $p_*(K_X + D) = p_*\mathcal{O}(-1) \otimes K_B = 0$. So $h^0(K_X + D) = 0$. Thus $\overline{P}_1 = 0$.

To get $\overline{P}_1 > 0$, we need $K_X + D$ to be effective.
